# 1 Chronicles Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 375v–376r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_009_page_001.jpg, 1CH_009_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** So all Israel was enrolled by genealogies, and these are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. And Judah was taken into exile in Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.

**2** Now the first to settle again in their possessions in their cities were Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants.

**3** And in Jerusalem lived some of the people of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh:

**4** Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, from the sons of Perez the son of Judah. **5** And of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons. **6** Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel, and their kinsmen — 690.

**7** Of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah; **8** Ibneiah the son of Jeroham; Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri; and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah. **9** Their kinsmen according to their generations were 956. All these were heads of fathers' houses.

**10** Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin, **11** and Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the chief officer of the house of God; **12** and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah; and Maasai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer. **13** Their kinsmen, heads of their fathers' houses — 1,760, able men for the work of the service of the house of God.

**14** Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari; **15** and Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph; **16** and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.

**17** The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their kinsmen. Shallum was the chief. **18** He was stationed previously at the king's gate on the east side. These were the gatekeepers of the camps of the sons of Levi.

**19** Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his kinsmen of his father's house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent. Their fathers had been over the camp of the LORD as keepers of the entrance. **20** And Phinehas the son of Eleazar was the chief officer over them in former times; the LORD was with him.

**21** Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

**22** All these, who were chosen as gatekeepers at the thresholds, were 212. They were enrolled by genealogies in their villages. David and Samuel the seer established them in their office of trust. **23** So they and their sons were in charge of the gates of the house of the LORD, that is, the house of the tent, as guards.

**24** The gatekeepers were on the four sides: east, west, north, and south. **25** And their kinsmen in their villages were obligated to come in every seven days, in turn, to be with them. **26** For the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were entrusted with the oversight of the chambers and the treasuries of the house of God. **27** They lodged around the house of God, for on them lay the duty of guarding, and they had charge of opening it every morning.

**28** Some of them had charge of the vessels of service, for they were counted when brought in and counted when taken out. **29** Others were appointed over the furniture and over all the holy vessels, also over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices. **30** Others, of the sons of the priests, prepared the mixing of the spices.

**31** Mattithiah, one of the Levites, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with making the flat cakes. **32** Also some of their kinsmen of the Kohathites had charge of the showbread, to prepare it every Sabbath.

**33** Now these are the singers, heads of fathers' houses of the Levites, living in the chambers of the temple, set free from other service, for they were on duty day and night.

**34** These were heads of fathers' houses of the Levites, according to their generations, chiefs. These lived in Jerusalem.

**35** In Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon, Jeiel, and the name of his wife was Maacah. **36** His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab, **37** Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth. **38** Mikloth fathered Shimeam. These also lived opposite their kinsmen in Jerusalem, with their kinsmen.

**39** Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal. **40** The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.

**41** The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz. **42** Ahaz fathered Jarah, and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri fathered Moza. **43** Moza fathered Binea, and Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.

**44** Azel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 9 closes the genealogical prologue (chs. 1-9) and opens the door to narrative. The chapter has three sections: (1) the summary of exile and return (vv.1-2); (2) the settlement list of the restored community (vv.3-34); and (3) the repeated Saulide genealogy (vv.35-44). The settlement list parallels Nehemiah 11 and establishes the post-exilic community as the legitimate continuation of pre-exilic Israel. The temple personnel sections (gatekeepers vv.17-27, supply managers vv.28-32, musicians v.33) reveal the Chronicler's deep interest in worship infrastructure. The word *emunah* (trust/faithfulness) appears twice in the gatekeeper section — these roles are positions of sacred trust, not mere employment. The Saulide genealogy repeated from ch.8 creates a deliberate bridge to ch.10 (Saul's death), transitioning from genealogy to narrative.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "treachery" vs. "unfaithfulness"
- **EMET:** "for-their-treachery [bema'alam]"
- **LOGOS:** "because of their unfaithfulness"
- **PNEUMA:** "because of their unfaithfulness"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "because of their unfaithfulness" — consistent with the ruling at 5:25. *Ma'al* rendered as "unfaithfulness" throughout.

### V.2 — "Netinim" rendering
- **EMET:** "the-Netinim [ha-netinim]" (transliteration)
- **LOGOS:** "the temple servants"
- **PNEUMA:** "temple servants"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the temple servants" — the English reader needs the functional meaning. *Netinim* ("given ones") were dedicated servants of the temple.

### V.11 — "nagid" rendering
- **EMET:** "prince [nagid] of-the-house of-God"
- **LOGOS:** "the chief officer of the house of God"
- **PNEUMA:** "the chief official of God's temple"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the chief officer of the house of God" — *nagid* in this priestly context means "chief officer" or "leader," not "prince" in the royal sense.

### V.22 — "Samuel the seer" vs. "Samuel the prophet"
- **EMET:** "Shemu'el the-seer [ha-ro'eh]"
- **LOGOS:** "Samuel the seer"
- **PNEUMA:** "Samuel the prophet"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Samuel the seer" — *ro'eh* specifically means "seer" (one who sees), not the more general *navi* (prophet). The distinction matters for the Chronicler.

### V.33 — "set free" vs. "exempt from other duties"
- **EMET:** "set-free [peturim]"
- **LOGOS:** "set free from other service"
- **PNEUMA:** "exempt from other duties"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "set free from other service" — *peturim* means released/exempted. "Set free from other service" conveys both the literal meaning and the reason.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
